=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- agents.md: line 2000 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: The text claims "every failback target keeps a 1M+ token window because reviewer prompts regularly exceed 250K tokens." Two of the six live failback targets named in the same sentence are below 1M: `deepseek/deepseek-v3.2` has `context_window: 128000` (128K) at `scripts/codex_model_catalog.json:267`, and `minimax/minimax-m2.5` has `context_window: 200000` (200K) at `scripts/codex_model_catalog.json:27`.
  WHY: No runtime code impact — this is a documentation defect. But an operator who reads this claim and relies on it may assume every failback target can safely receive a 250K+ token reviewer prompt. When the circuit breaker fires for the deepseek or minimax slot, the failback target silently truncates the prompt (the `truncation_policy` in the catalog caps at 1M bytes but OpenRouter imposes its own limit at the model's context window), and the review run continues with a truncated prompt instead of failing visibly.
- scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh: line 149 | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  PROBLEM: `reviewer_turn_count` counts turns using `grep -cF '"type":"step_start"'` — a fixed-string match that depends on OpenCode's current JSON serialization format (no spaces after colons).
  WHY: The guard silently stops counting turns. A looping reviewer that exceeds 120 turns would continue until HEARTBEAT_MAX_WALL (2+ hours) kills it, which is exactly the failure mode the guard was built to prevent.
- scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh: lines 165-181 | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  PROBLEM: The `reviewer_tool_repeat_detected` Python parser exits on the first unparseable event line (line 177: `sys.exit(1)` on JSON parse/access failure).
  WHY: When an unparseable line falls within the last `REVIEWER_TOOL_REPEAT_LIMIT` tool_use events, preceding identical tool calls go undetected and the guard reports no repeat.
- scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh: lines 165-181 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The `case "${wd_reason}" in max_steps|tool_repeat)` override that forces `cmd_rc=143` when OpenCode exited cleanly after a loop guard fired is reachable; the watchdog runs in a background subshell and its `exit 145/146` only terminates the subshell, not the parent.
  WHY: No defect — the code is correct. The override catches the case where `_reviewer_kill_pid` is called with an empty `cpid`, OpenCode continues, and `wait` returns a potentially clean exit code.
- scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh: lines 3988-4004 | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  PROBLEM: The new `max_steps` and `tool_repeat` watchdog kill paths inherit the same `cpid="$(cat "${codex_pid_file}" 2>/dev/null || true)"` pattern already used by `idle_timeout` (line 3975) and `max_wall` (line 3983).
  WHY: In practice this race cannot manifest for either new guard. The turn cap requires 121+ turns before firing, each involving at least one API round-trip (seconds), so by the time the guard trips the PID file was written hundreds of seconds ago.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- agents.md: 2000 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: Documentation incorrectly claims "every failback target keeps a 1M+ token window".
  WHY: Failback models like `deepseek/deepseek-v3.2` (128K context) and `minimax/minimax-m2.5` (200K context) are significantly below the 1M threshold. Operators relying on this claim may configure failback settings that lead to silent prompt truncation and degraded review quality.
- scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh: 149 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: `reviewer_turn_count` uses `grep -cF '"type":"step_start"'` to count turns.
  WHY: This heuristic relies on exact JSON serialization and formatting. Any change in OpenCode's JSON output (e.g., whitespace, field order) will cause this count to become zero, silently disabling the `REVIEWER_MAX_STEPS` guard.
- scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh: 162-181 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: `reviewer_tool_repeat_detected` exits with status 1 on the first unparseable JSON line in the event stream.
  WHY: If the event log contains a truncated or malformed line, the parser will fail open, ignoring all preceding tool calls in the window and failing to detect looping behavior.
- scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh: 4114-4121 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The `case "${wd_reason}" in max_steps|tool_repeat)` override in `reviewer_classify_retryable_failure` is unreachable.
  WHY: The watchdog kill paths in `execute_reviewer_attempt` execute `exit` before control returns to the post-wait section. This dead code misleads maintainers into trusting a cleanup path that does not exist.
- scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh: 3989-4003 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The new loop-guard kill paths read the PID from `${codex_pid_file}` immediately, racing with process initialization.
  WHY: If the watchdog polls before the process initializes and writes its PID, `cpid` is empty. `_reviewer_kill_pid` with an empty PID no-ops, leaving the looping reviewer running until `HEARTBEAT_MAX_WALL` fires, defeating the loop guard.
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- agents.md:2000, the sentence starting "The live-roster mapping file covers … `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro -> deepseek/deepseek-v3.2` … and `z-ai/glm-5.2 -> z-ai/glm-5.3-flashx`; every failback target keeps a 1M+ token window because reviewer prompts regularly exceed 250K tokens." | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: The claim that "every failback target keeps a 1M+ token window" is factually wrong for two of the live-roster failback targets. `scripts/codex_model_catalog.json:267` sets `deepseek/deepseek-v3.2` `context_window: 128000` and `scripts/codex_model_catalog.json:27` sets `minimax/minimax-m2.5` `context_window: 200000`; both are well below the 1M threshold the prose asserts and below the 250K-token reviewer-prompt figure it uses as the rationale.
  WHY: An operator reading the doc while configuring `vars.REVIEW_TIER_STANDARD_REVIEWER_SLUGS` or sizing failback budgets for a 250K-token reviewer prompt will assume both targets can absorb that prompt. When the deepseek/minimax failback fires, OpenCode silently truncates the prompt at the model's context window, the slot "succeeds" at producing a low-quality review, and nothing in the runtime signals that the fallback is undersized.
- scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh: scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh:153-181 (`reviewer_tool_repeat_detected`) | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The header comment says "Unreadable or partial events never count as a repeat (fail open)," but the implementation does the opposite on a malformed line. The Python inner script is `for raw_line in sys.stdin: try: ... except (ValueError, KeyError, TypeError, AttributeError): sys.exit(1)`, which exits on the FIRST unparseable event regardless of how many valid, identical repeats precede it.
  WHY: The guard runs on the last `REVIEWER_TOOL_REPEAT_LIMIT` `tool_use` events (`tail -n "${repeat_limit}"`). If those N events are e.g. 9 identical `grep` calls and 1 truncated line, the parser exits 1 after the 9th valid event and never reaches the comparison; the loop is reported as not a repeat and the watchdog does not fire `tool_repeat`.
- scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh: scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh:144-151 (`reviewer_turn_count`) | severity=high | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: `grep -cF '"type":"step_start"' "${structured_file}"` matches an exact, unspaced substring of the OpenCode 1.18.23 JSON event shape. A future OpenCode release that changes whitespace, field ordering, or the literal `step_start` token (e.g. `step_start` -> `step-start`, or `"type": "step_start"` with a space) would silently produce a count of zero on every poll, the `-gt` comparison would never fire, and `REVIEWER_MAX_STEPS` would become a no-op while continuing to advertise itself as the safeguard.
  WHY: After a routine OpenCode upgrade, a looping reviewer (exactly the failure mode this guard was added for) would no longer be capped because the count never crosses the limit. The previous "every call looked like progress to the idle watchdog" failure mode re-appears; only the wall-clock kill remains.
